body:
Worker rule (Termal::Opus2, 2026-10-30 ~15:52Z; my own slip, corrected by Fable2 #3281).

Never open the live host's stores directly: ~/.termal/coordination.sqlite, ~/.termal/termal.sqlite or any other ~/.termal/*.sqlite. That includes read-only opens (`sqlite3 ...?mode=ro`, Python's sqlite3 with uri mode=ro).

The standing rule is supported surfaces only. A read-only open still contends with the running host's database files and locks, the WAL and shm in particular.

What I did: after a restart, to confirm the coordination floor 7 version string, I opened coordination.sqlite with Python sqlite3 mode=ro.

Use instead:
- supported API reads (/api/health, /api/sessions/..., /api/engram/named-roots);
- behavioural proof, for example mailbox reads and writes working proves the coordination store opened;
- host-lifecycle.jsonl, which is an append-only log, for heartbeats.
If an exact internal value is ever needed, ask the coordinator for a supported read path rather than opening the store.
